title: M0 — the real slice: substrate + exemplar skill + Tier-0 verifier + tier gate (40-bit toy curve end to end)
description:
WHY THIS MILESTONE EXISTS
Cairn is a research harness whose epistemics are immutable and whose strategy is mutable (PLAN §0; CLAUDE.md). M0 builds the one vertical slice everything else plugs into: a content-addressed substrate (SQLite + BLAKE3), one exemplar skill built end to end (content-addressed I/O, captured seed, known-answer self-test, declared cost profile), the Tier-0 verifier (`xP == Q` in a subprocess), and the tier gate with its gate bundle + pin. "Everything else plugs into this shape — get it right once, the verifier included." Build M0 before adding another design layer: a running 40-bit slice reveals more than more architecture.

OPERATOR DECISIONS THAT BIND M0 (confirmed 2026-08-21; recorded in PLAN §16)
(1) PARI-only arithmetic at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check through 50 bits; the gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS enters as the *implementation* axis at M1.
(2) One 60-bit rho measured with cypari2 at M0 (bead m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15); a compiled baseline is funded at M1 only if the interpreted rung cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget.
(5) Skill yanks and `salt` issuance are human-only, like waivers — at M0 the `yank_records`/`salts` rows therefore carry the human-path digest+offset columns (schema only; behavior M1).
(8) No separate OS user for the orchestrator before M3; at M0 the gate-bundle pin and the attestation file are protected by file mode/flags only, and the grounding brief records exactly what that does and does not refuse (probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6/APFS: mode 0644 + `uappnd` lets the owner append and refuses overwrite, `r+`, truncate AND `chmod` while the flag stands; 0444 + `uappnd` refuses append too, so the attestation file is 0644+uappnd and the pin is 0444+uappnd; the owner can still `chflags nouappnd` — the one-user gap).
(9) A ticket carries its gate-bundle hash; a mismatch re-mints the ticket.

STACK FACTS M0 STANDS ON (probed on this Mac 2026-08-21; research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md)
PARI/GP 2.17.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp (the shell has `alias gp='git push'` — always use the full path); cypari2 2.2.4 bundles libpari 2.17.2 and produced bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries to gp for the toy-curve search; `ellcard` is milliseconds through 50 bits, ≈75 ms/curve at 60 bits and overflows the default 8 MB PARI stack (use `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` / `gp -s 64M`); gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow) with the message on stderr, zero-fills missing arguments, and writes nothing to stderr on a successful quiet run (so the verifier's empty-stderr accept predicate is satisfiable); the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`/`ellsea(E,1)` but not by ≤ 50-bit `ellcard`, so `toy_curve` pins its call sequence (cairn-m0-e0s.6); under SQLite's rollback journal only `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` blocks a reader (the WAL probe's control arm, cairn-m0-e0s.2); Sage absent; elan/lean absent. M0 re-executes the facts it relies on as tests and records the rest (WAL, busy timeout, append-only flag, write boundary) — bead m0-grounding-probes (cairn-m0-e0s.2).

DONE WHEN (PLAN §13 M0):
- the exemplar skill `toy_curve(bits, seed)` runs on a 40-bit toy curve; a deterministic M0 fixture (an integration fixture, not a second research skill) derives `x` and `Q = xP` from that output; the subprocess verifier accepts that pair, rejects a one-coordinate and a one-scalar negative fixture, classifies a forced backend crash as FAIL, and refuses — before the subprocess spawns — a submission that names its own `(P, Q)` rather than the statement node's;
- the generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result and gate-run record are hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged substrate nodes;
- the tier gate refuses a fixture launch declaring a tier two above its ticket and records `TierRefused`; a gate run against a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed;
- a write to the pin and a write to the attestation file, each attempted as the orchestrator's process user, are refused by the operating system, and a `review_verdict` row whose digest matches no attestation record is absent to `justify`;
- `justify` returns STRONG-EMPIRICAL from a synthetic `ladder_table` evidence node with verdict KEEP whose attempt carries a passed reproducibility record, returns the CONJECTURE ceiling for the same table with that record absent or its grade `AuditOnly`, returns a coverage violation when the table's population does not cover the statement's scope, and returns a lattice violation when a synthetic `statistical` node is offered for PROVEN, against a synthetic statement hash;
- a blob unreachable from the roots table is collectable while a rooted one is not;
- the first gate self-tests run before the gates: the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

SCHEMA-ONLY AT M0 (behavior exercised at M1): budget-ceiling enforcement, escrow reserve/spend/release, yank reach and `disowned` propagation. M0 has a fixture writing and reading each such column. A behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture, not a slice.

ENGINEERING RULES FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Integration test first (real PARI via cypari2, real gp subprocess, real SQLite file), unit tests second: unit tests cover the pure predicates (canonical encoding, the verifier's pre-spawn validator and accept predicate, the tier-gate predicate, `justify`'s coverage comparator and kind→class map, the runner's status mapping); e2e is `tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py`. No mock may stand in for the gate under test; a planted fault (a monkeypatched backend answer, a killed child) is not a mock of the gate.
- Logging: one logger (`src/cairn/log.py`, bead cairn-m0-e0s.1) used by every CLI and every gate decision; each record names the step, the input hashes, the `gate_runs` row id where one exists, the verdict with its reasons and the timing; `--log DEBUG` (or `CAIRN_LOG=DEBUG`) adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr digests; tests assert on the log records wherever a verdict is involved (pytest caplog), so a silent gate is a failing test.
- Python via `uv` only (`uv run pytest`, `uv add`); never bare pip/python; subprocesses use `sys.executable`.
- Zero explanatory comments in code; names carry meaning.
- Every child carries a positive observable, a planted negative (a fixture that must FAIL), and a No-Claim line (what green does not prove).
- Closure of a child is a claim until its commands are re-executed at close; paste command + output in the close comment. The epic closes only when `uv run pytest` is green on a fresh clone and `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` (bead m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14) produces the four nodes.

SHARED FIXTURES (named once, used by several beads): `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` — the 60-bit (p,a,b,n,P) that the grounding brief's bench.gp yields at bits=60 seed=1, generated once with gp and committed by cairn-m0-e0s.1; the stack-fact test (.1), the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (.8), the gate plan's crash fixture (.11) read it, and cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60, 1)` reproduces it. `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` — one brief with sections written by .2 (stack facts), .6 (tries table), .15 (rho at 60 bits).

NOT IN M0: the ladder, baseline skills, Lean gate, workers, orchestrator, parallel tracks (M1–M4 epics). The research tree is never pre-decomposed into beads (CLAUDE.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads closed with their own evidence re-executed at close.
- `uv run pytest` green on a fresh clone (integration + unit); output attached to the close comment.
- `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` writes four nodes (generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result, gate-run record) with content hashes, self-test references and cost tags; re-running with the same seed reproduces the generator output hash (Replayable).
- Every done-when bullet maps to a named test that was run, with command and output in the close comment.
- Planted negative (epic level): each planted fixture must fail or be refused — the verifier's `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures (cairn-m0-e0s.8/.11), the tier-two-above launch (.10), the bundle whose hash ≠ pin (.10), the forged `review_verdict` digest (.10/.12), the uncertified revision (.7/.10/.14), the `statistical`-for-PROVEN offer (.12), the orphan blob that must be collectable while the rooted one survives (.13); any of these passing silently fails the epic.
- No-Claim: M0 green proves the slice's gates refuse the planted fixtures on this Mac; it proves nothing about ECDLP, about any research claim, or about behavior under a second OS user / Linux container.

title: M0: uv project scaffold + real-PARI smoke test (cypari2 in-process + gp subprocess + 60-bit stack fact)
description:
WHY: every later bead runs real PARI through two builds — cypari2 in-process for skills, /opt/homebrew/bin/gp as the verifier subprocess — and real SQLite. Nothing downstream is testable until the toolchain is pinned and a real call succeeds under `uv run`.

WHAT
- `uv init --package` layout: `pyproject.toml` (name `cairn`, Python ≥3.14 — cypari2 2.2.4 ships a 3.14 wheel per the grounding brief), `src/cairn/`, console script `cairn` (argparse is enough).
- Deps: `cypari2` (bundles libpari 2.17.2), `blake3`; dev: `pytest`. `gmpy2` is added at M1 only (operator decision 1).
- Dirs: `tests/integration/` (real PARI/gp/SQLite; the default suite), `tests/unit/`, `tests/e2e/`, `tests/vectors/`, `bundle/` (gate-bundle source), `deploy/` (built bundle + pin + attestation file; gitignored except a README), `var/` (runtime DBs; gitignored). `.gitignore`: `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `var/`, `deploy/*.sqlite`, `deploy/*.pin`, `deploy/*.log`.
- `src/cairn/pari.py`: one shared cypari2 handle; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000, silent=True)` exactly once at import (the 60-bit `ellcard` overflows the 8 MB default — PROVEN by probe; `silent=True` keeps PARI's stack-size notice off the harness's stderr, as the grounding brief's `bench_cypari2.py` does); `GP_BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp"` with an existence check raising a typed error; `pari_versions()` returning `pari.version()` and the cypari2 version (they feed the environment-manifest digest in bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); thin wrappers `ellcard(E)` / `ellsea(E, early_abort)` so a later test can plant a disagreement at one seam (cairn-m0-e0s.6). Never call gp through a shell.
- `src/cairn/log.py`: the one logger every CLI and gate decision uses — structured records on stderr `{ts, step, ids/hashes, verdict, reasons, wall_ms}`; level from `--log LEVEL` or `CAIRN_LOG` (default INFO); DEBUG adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; never logs substrate paths into a skill's environment. Tests assert on records via pytest caplog.
- Shared fixture: `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` = `{bits:60, seed:1, p, a, b, n, P:[x,y]}` as decimal strings, generated ONCE in gp with EXACTLY the call sequence cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins for bits > 50 (the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E,1)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`, so any other call order yields a different curve — probed 2026-08-21): `setrand(1); p = randomprime([2^59, 2^60]); tries = 0; while(1, a = random(p); b = random(p); if((4*a^3 + 27*b^2) % p == 0, next); tries++; E = ellinit([a,b], p); n = ellsea(E, 1); if(n && isprime(n), break)); if(ellcard(E) != n, error("confirm")); P = random(E)` run as `/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M gen60.gp`; the grounding brief's mode-1 row predicts `tries = 45` at seed 1 and the file records it; committed with `origin: author_supplied`, the gp script (`tests/vectors/gen60.gp`) and the tries count in the file; the stack-fact smoke test (c) below, the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (cairn-m0-e0s.8) and the gate plan's crash fixture (cairn-m0-e0s.11) read it; cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60,1)` reproduces it bit-for-bit.
- Smoke tests (integration, `tests/integration/test_smoke.py`):
  (a) cypari2: `ellinit([-3,1],5)` → `ellcard` = 7 (PARI user manual usersch3.tex:29031-29032, upstream_vendored);
  (b) gp subprocess: `subprocess.run([GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s","64M"], input="print(ellcard(ellinit([-3,1],5)))")` → stdout `7`, rc 0;
  (c) stack fact: `ellcard` on the committed 60-bit curve (`tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json`) succeeds under allocatemem (cypari2) and under `gp -s 64M` and equals the vector's `n`; control: the same under `gp -s 8M` fails with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0 (the gp exit-0-on-fatal fact).
- Unit tests (`tests/unit/test_pari_module.py`): `run_gp` builds argv `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",<stack>]` and passes `shell=False`; a missing `GP_BIN` (monkeypatched path) raises the typed error before any spawn; `log.py` emits a parseable record at INFO and adds digests only at DEBUG.
- `uv run cairn --version` prints the version; `uv run cairn --version --log DEBUG` emits at least one structured record on stderr.

DESIGN: the PARI handle lives in one module so allocatemem runs once; all gp invocations go through `cairn.pari.run_gp(args, stdin)` returning (rc, stdout, stderr) so later beads share one spawn path; all logging goes through `cairn.log.get(step)` so every bead's records have one shape.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_smoke.py tests/unit/test_pari_module.py -q` green; three smoke tests visible: cypari2 ellcard=7, gp subprocess prints 7, 60-bit ellcard on the committed vector succeeds under the 64 MB stack and matches the vector's `n`; `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` committed with its generating gp script (`tests/vectors/gen60.gp`) and `tries: 45` (the grounding brief's mode-1 row; a different count means the call sequence drifted from the one cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins, and the smoke test asserts the count); `uv run cairn --version --log DEBUG` prints the version and one structured log record.
- Planted negative: 60-bit `ellcard` under `gp -s 8M` must fail with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0, asserted as the expected failure shape; if it unexpectedly succeeds the test fails (the stack fact changed and the verifier's stack ceiling needs re-grounding); a monkeypatched missing `GP_BIN` must raise the typed error with zero spawns.
- `grep -r "which gp\|'gp'" src/` finds nothing; the only gp path is `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`.
- No-Claim: green proves the toolchain loads and one known curve order computes; it proves nothing about any skill, gate or timing profile; the 60-bit vector is author-generated (its order is re-checked by the test, not vendored).
notes:
BEAD ALIASES → IDS (the descriptions name beads by alias; these are the br ids): m0-scaffold-smoke = cairn-m0-e0s.1; m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2; m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4; m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5; m0-toy-curve-skill = cairn-m0-e0s.6; m0-skill-selftest-cert = cairn-m0-e0s.7; m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8; m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9; m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13; m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14; m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15; m1-ladder = cairn-m1-cqt.1; m1-baseline-skills = cairn-m1-cqt.2; m1-planted-corpus = cairn-m1-cqt.3; m1-budget-escrow-yank = cairn-m1-cqt.4; m1-formalization-gate = cairn-m1-cqt.5; m1-worker-dispatch-canary = cairn-m1-cqt.6; m1-human-queue-review = cairn-m1-cqt.7; m1-router-ledger-hunt-repro = cairn-m1-cqt.8.

TOOLCHAIN FACT (probed 2026-08-21 in a scratch uv project): ~/.config/uv/uv.toml sets a corporate Artifactory index as default and it times out off-network; the cairn pyproject.toml must pin PyPI itself:
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.org/simple"
default = true
With that, `uv add cypari2 blake3` and `uv add --dev pytest` resolve (Python 3.14.0 arm64, cypari2 2.2.4 / libpari 2.17.2, blake3 1.0.9); cypari2 has no `__version__` — read versions via importlib.metadata; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` prints a line unless silent=True.

title: M0: gate bundle (separate read-only SQLite, content-addressed) + deployment pin (0444+append-only) + attestation file (0644+append-only) + attestation digest/offset check + tier gate predicate (TierRefused; bundle≠pin fails closed; uncertified/yanked refused; ticket bundle-hash mismatch re-mints) + OS write-boundary tests + waiver-cannot-advance fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §5): a gate that silently fails open manufactures the appearance of enforcement. The gate bundle is content-addressed, opened read-only by the orchestrator process, its hash pinned at deployment in an operator-owned file the process user cannot write, and recorded in every gate-run record; a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed whoever rewrote it. The tier gate reads only launch-supplied inputs (cost profile at inputs, budget, hypothesis key/method identity) plus substrate-resolved ones (self-test standing, ticket) and judges against gate-owned objects; a refusal is a `TierRefused` record, not an exception to retry around. Operator decisions 8 (one OS user at M0 → mode/flags only; what that refuses is recorded by bead m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2) and 9 (ticket carries bundle hash; mismatch ⇒ re-mint) bind.

WHAT (`src/cairn/bundle.py`: build, pin, `GateBundle`; `src/cairn/attest.py`: `attest init/append`, `attestation_record_matches`, `visible_review_verdicts`; `src/cairn/tiergate.py`: `TierGate`)
- `bundle/*.json` source: `verifier {backend_path:"/opt/homebrew/bin/gp", stack_ceiling:"64M", timeout_s:30, accept:"rc==0 && stdout==OK && stderr==''"}`; `tiers {boundary_table:[{tier:0,max_core_s:1},{tier:1,max_core_s:3600},{tier:2,max_core_s:3600000},{tier:3,max_core_s:null}] (one unit, core-seconds, throughout; M0 defaults, CONJECTURE; 3 600 000 core-s is the ≈10³ core-hour Tier-2/3 edge of PLAN §5; a launch's tier is the first row whose max its production cost does not exceed), ceiling_multiplier:4, tier1_cumulative_edge:null}` (edge set at M1, decision 10); `gate_plan` (ordered steps with expected results — bead m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; its crash fixture embeds the committed 60-bit instance from `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` as decimal strings); `waivable_checks: []` (no admission gate is waivable; the waiver fixture consults this set); `auditor {f:0.01,bits:20}`; `lean {permitted_axioms:["propext","Classical.choice","Quot.sound"]}` (stored, unused until M1); `role_templates:{}`, `allow_lists:{}` (M1).
- `uv run cairn bundle build --src bundle/ --out deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`: one row per object (kind, canonical bytes, hash); bundle hash = H('cairn/gate-bundle/v1' ‖ sorted (kind,hash) pairs); deterministic (build twice → same hash). `uv run cairn bundle pin --bundle ... --pin deploy/gate-bundle.pin` writes the hash, chmods pin and bundle 0444 and sets `uappnd` on the pin (macOS; probed 2026-08-21: with the flag standing the owner's `chmod` is refused too; re-pinning is the operator's act and needs `chflags nouappnd` first). `uv run cairn attest init deploy/attestations.log` creates the file mode 0644 and sets `uappnd` (appendable by the owner, not overwritable, not truncatable, not re-modable while flagged; 0444 would refuse the append — cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 3); elsewhere than macOS it logs loudly and skips the flag.
- `GateBundle.open(path, pin_path)`: opens `file:...?mode=ro`; recomputes the hash from rows; compares to the pin; mismatch → `BundlePinMismatch`, and every gate run refuses with a `gate_runs` row `gate='bundle_open', result='refused', reasons=['bundle-hash-ne-pin']`.
- `attestation_record_matches(file, offset, digest) -> bool`: reads the length-prefixed canonical record at `offset`, compares BLAKE3; `visible_review_verdicts(statement_hash)` filters rows through it (used by bead m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; the same function serves `yank_records`/`salts` at M1). Operator append path: `uv run cairn attest append --kind review_verdict ...` appends the canonical record and mirrors the substrate row with digest+offset (at M0 the same OS user runs both; the boundary is the file mode/flag + the digest rule).
- `TierGate.admit(launch) -> Admitted | TierRefused`; launch = `{cost_profile, inputs, budget_remaining, hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, skill_identity_hash, declared_tier}`; resolves `certified(skill_identity)` and `not yanked(skill_identity)` (predicates in cairn-m0-e0s.4); selects the ticket (Tier 0: none; Tier 1: a hypothesis object, plus the claim statement node where a claim exists, recorded in the substrate — the §8 presence check and the §7 statement pre-filters that also condition the Tier-1 ticket arrive at M1; Tier 2/3 kinds are M1 — absent ⇒ refuse); refuses when `declared_tier > ticket_tier + 1` (`tier_refusals` row), when declared tier < the tier the boundary table assigns the production cost at the launch's inputs, when uncertified or yanked, when declared production + verification cost > remaining budget; every decision is a `gate_runs` row (gate='tier_gate', result admitted|refused) with bundle hash + pin hash; a ticket whose recorded bundle hash ≠ current bundle hash → refused `ticket-bundle-mismatch` (re-mint, decision 9). Every decision logs (hypothesis key, declared tier, ticket tier, reasons) through `cairn.log`.
- Waiver fixture: a waiver record appended through the attestation path does NOT produce a ticket or admit a tier (admission gates are non-waivable, §4; `waivable_checks` is empty). The claim half of the same §4 fixture — a waiver moves no tag — is `justify`'s own planted test (cairn-m0-e0s.12).
TESTS (integration, real files under tmp_path; `tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py`, `tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py`): build+pin; open OK; edit one row in a writable copy of the bundle → open refuses, gate_runs row says why; `open(pin,'w')`, `open(pin,'a')`, `os.chmod(pin,0o644)` → PermissionError; `open(attestations,'w')` and `os.truncate` → PermissionError; `open(attestations,'a')` succeeds and the mirrored review_verdict row is visible only when digest/offset match (forge a row with a wrong digest → absent); launch declaring tier 2 with a Tier-0 ticket → TierRefused row; tier 1 with hypothesis object recorded → Admitted; uncertified skill → refused; yanked skill (a yank_records row) → refused; production cost above the Tier-1 boundary declared as tier 1 → refused; declared cost above the remaining budget → refused; ticket with stale bundle hash → refused; waiver → no ticket.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py`, pure): the predicate's truth table over (declared tier, ticket tier, boundary-table tier at cost, certified, yanked, budget ok, ticket bundle matches) — each refusal reason reached by exactly the rows that should reach it; the boundary-table lookup at its edges (1, 3600, 3 600 000 core-s: a cost exactly at an edge stays in the lower tier, one unit above it moves up).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py -q` green; `uv run cairn bundle build` twice → identical bundle hash; deploy/ artifacts created with modes 0444 (bundle), 0444+uappnd (pin) and 0644+uappnd (attestations), asserted by `os.stat` and `ls -lO`.
- Planted negative: modified bundle → fail closed with a gate_runs row; tier-two-above → TierRefused recorded; pin write and pin chmod → PermissionError; attestation overwrite/truncate → PermissionError; forged review_verdict digest → absent; waiver → no ticket; stale-bundle ticket → refused; yanked/uncertified → refused. Any of these passing silently fails the bead.

title: M0: justify(evidence, statement_hash): kind→max-class map, producer-standing ceiling, coverage check (interval containment / categorical equality / assumption ⊆), lattice violations, review_verdict digest rule, refuted-version rule, append-only attributed tag history
description:
WHY (PLAN §7): the tag is derived, never set. Each evidence kind has a maximum class; `justify` checks the evidence's declared target names the exact statement hash, its declared population is a superset of the statement's scope and its assumptions a subset of the statement's, and returns a typed justification or a lattice/coverage violation — never a boolean. A weaker class may inform, never justify. Every tag transition is an append-only attributed tag_history row with an evidence pointer. PROVEN needs a `lean_artifact` AND an `approve` `review_verdict` on the same statement hash whose digest matches the attestation file (else the row is absent).

WHAT (`src/cairn/justify.py`; tables from bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5)
- `justify(evidence, statement, ctx) -> Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation | Absent | Pending`. Classes are totally ordered SPECULATION < CONJECTURE < STRONG-EMPIRICAL < PROVEN.
- Kind → max class: `lean_artifact` + visible `approve` verdict on the same statement hash → PROVEN (without it → `Pending(human_review)`, claim stays at its pre-review tag); `ladder_table` verdict KEEP — or KEEP_IN_SAMPLE when the statement's `scope.size_interval ⊆ evidence.in_sample_sizes` — whose own attempt carries a passed reproducibility record (`repro_records.passed = 1` reached through `evidence.repro_record_hash`) → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; same table with the record absent or grade `AuditOnly` → CONJECTURE ceiling; any other table verdict → justifies nothing; `statistical` / `repro_node` → ≤ STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the declared population, EXCEPT for a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model (`claim_statements.quantities.cost_model IS NOT NULL`) → CONJECTURE ceiling; `model_proof` → ≤ CONJECTURE; `counterexample_hunt_record` SURVIVED → CONJECTURE (a ticket, not a promotion), KILLED → the statement moves to terminal `refuted` with the evidence pointer.
- Producer-standing ceiling: producer is a certified skill revision (its `skill_certificates.selftest_summary`, cairn-m0-e0s.4/.7) with no STRONG-EMPIRICAL basis covering the attempt's inputs — every `corpus_origins` entry `author_supplied`, `randomized_arm` false, and no `cross_check` whose `independent_range` contains the inputs → cap at CONJECTURE; a gate-bundle producer or a gate run is not capped by this rule.
- Coverage: `population.target_family == scope.target_family`; numeric intervals of the population contain the statement's (size and every parameter range); `population.assumptions ⊆ statement.assumptions`; otherwise CoverageViolation (typed: which field).
- Disowned evidence (attempt `disowned_at` not null) → Absent; an `AuditOnly` node (by `effective_grade`, cairn-m0-e0s.4) → the CONJECTURE ceiling, never Absent and never higher (inadmissible above it, §3 — the done-when's AuditOnly case). Refuted statement + any positive class → LatticeViolation. A class offered above the kind's maximum (e.g. `statistical` for PROVEN) → LatticeViolation.
- `derive_tag(statement_hash)` = strongest class justified by any evidence node targeting it; writes a tag_history row (actor 'gate:justify', evidence pointer, typed justification); a downgrade requires an evidence pointer; nothing edited in place.
- `review_verdicts` visible only through `attestation_record_matches` (`src/cairn/attest.py`, bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10). A waiver is not evidence: `evidence_nodes.kind` admits no waiver kind, `justify` reads the attestation file for `review_verdict` records and nothing else, and `derive_tag` is unchanged by a waiver record naming the statement hash — the claim half of §4's waiver-cannot-advance fixture (the tier half is cairn-m0-e0s.10's).
- CLI: `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and the justifying evidence hash. Logging: every `justify` call logs (statement hash, evidence hash, kind, result type, class or violation field) and every `derive_tag` logs the transition through `cairn.log`.

UNIT (`tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py`, pure): the coverage comparator (interval containment incl. equal endpoints, categorical equality, assumption subset incl. empty set); the kind→max-class table; the class order; the producer-standing rule over synthetic summaries.

- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_justify.py tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py -q` green with every done-when case named in the test ids; `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and justifying evidence hash.
- Planted negative: statistical→PROVEN must be a LatticeViolation; missing or failed repro must cap at CONJECTURE; forged verdict digest must not yield PROVEN; a coverage gap must be a CoverageViolation; an all-`author_supplied` producer must be capped; a waiver record must move no tag. SQLite WAL (`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py`): file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` returns `wal`; the writer holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` plus one uncommitted INSERT and a second connection's SELECT returns (WAL readers never wait on a writer). Control: the same under `journal_mode=DELETE` → the reader's SELECT raises `OperationalError: database is locked` after its timeout. The writer MUST open with `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` — probed 2026-08-21 (Python 3.14.3 sqlite3, SQLite 3.52.0): under DELETE a plain `BEGIN` or `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holding an uncommitted INSERT leaves the reader unblocked (the writer holds RESERVED and readers still take SHARED), so the control arm would agree with the treatment and the probe would fail by its own rule; only EXCLUSIVE blocks readers, and under WAL all three BEGIN kinds leave the reader free.
2. Busy timeout: A holds a write txn; B with `PRAGMA busy_timeout=500` attempts a write → waits ≈0.5 s then `OperationalError: database is locked`; with A committing after 0.2 s, B succeeds. Record measured waits.
3. Append-only flag (`tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py`, macOS `chflags uappnd` on APFS), on a file owned by the current user. Pre-probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6 (the test must reproduce this table): mode 0644 + `uappnd`: `open(path,'a')`+write succeeds, `os.open(O_WRONLY|O_APPEND)` succeeds, `open(path,'w')` → EPERM, `open(path,'r+')` → EPERM, `os.truncate` → EPERM, `os.chmod` by the owner → EPERM while the flag stands; mode 0444 + `uappnd`: append → EACCES (the mode denies write before the flag is consulted), overwrite/truncate/chmod → EPERM; mode 0444 without the flag: every write → EACCES but the owner's `chmod` succeeds; mode 0644 without the flag: everything succeeds (control). Consequence: the attestation file is 0644 + `uappnd` (appendable, not overwritable, not re-modable while flagged), the pin is 0444 + `uappnd` (nothing writes it, nothing re-modes it while flagged). Record honestly: with ONE OS user (operator decision 8) the same user can `chflags nouappnd` and then chmod/truncate, so at M0 the flag refuses truncation and re-moding by the process but does not bind against a process that clears it — that half is OPEN until M3 introduces the second OS user; the Linux equivalent (`chattr +a`) is OPEN until the M1 container exists.
4. Write boundary: pin file 0444 + `uappnd` → `open(pin,'w')`, `open(pin,'a')`, `os.truncate(pin)`, `os.chmod(pin, 0o644)` all raise PermissionError for the (non-root) owner; attestation file 0644 + `uappnd` → `open(...,'w')`/`'r+'`/truncate/chmod raise, `open(...,'a')` by the same user succeeds (record: at M0 "cannot write" = cannot overwrite/truncate/re-mode; an append by the harness process is not refused until the two-user shape — the digest/offset rule in bead m0-justify (cairn-m0-e0s.12) is what makes a harness-appended forgery useless, and bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) tests that). Control: after `chflags nouappnd` the owner's chmod succeeds — the recorded gap.
5. gp facts (`tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py`): gp exits 0 on `1/0` with the message on stderr; a 3-arg user function called with 2 args runs with the third zero-filled; a successful run under `gp -q -f -s 64M <file.gp>` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr (probed 2026-08-21: stdout `OK`, rc 0 — the empty-stderr accept predicate of cairn-m0-e0s.8 is satisfiable); `quit(1)` yields rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; a 60-bit `ellcard` under `-s 8M` yields rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr; reference grounding brief pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §3.
6. PARI PRNG consumption (same test file; the fact cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins its call sequence on): after `setrand(s)` and a fixed prefix of draws, `random(2^64)` is unchanged by an intervening 40-bit `ellcard(E)` but changed by an intervening 40-bit `ellsea(E)`, and changed by an intervening 60-bit `ellcard(E)` or `ellsea(E,1)` (probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4); the test asserts each of the four comparisons in gp and in cypari2 (libpari 2.17.2).

DESIGN: the tests are the executable record; the brief is written by hand from their output with tags. Probes 3–4 skip with an explicit reason when not on macOS (the M1 Linux container gets its own probe bead). No generator script for the brief. Every probe logs its command and observed output through `cairn.log` at INFO so the brief's rows can be copied from the test log.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py -q` green on this Mac; `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` exists with one row per fact (fact, tag, command, observed output, date, OS/FS), including the four-row mode×flag table of probe 3, the chmod-refused-while-flagged row, the BEGIN-kind × journal-mode reader table of probe 1 and the PRNG-consumption rows of probe 6.
- Planted negative: each probe has a control arm doing the same operation without the protection (no WAL / no timeout / no flag / mode 0644) asserting the opposite outcome; a probe whose control and treatment agree fails (probe 1's writer therefore holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` — under plain `BEGIN` the DELETE-mode reader reads and the probe fails by design); the 0444+uappnd append must FAIL (EACCES) — if it succeeds the attestation-file mode rule in cairn-m0-e0s.10 is wrong and the test fails.

title: M0: canonical typed encoding + BLAKE3 content addressing: recipe key, hypothesis key, identity bundle, environment manifest; known-answer vectors for both keys
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): REFUTED-by-hash and every cache hit are exactly as sound as the canonicalizer — two logically equal recipes that hash differently are a bug that silently under-reports dead ends. The canonicalizer's known-answer vectors are one of the first gate self-tests (§13 M0) and run before any gate.

WHAT (`src/cairn/canon.py`, `src/cairn/keys.py`)
- Canonical encoding: typed, domain-separated; fields in fixed declared order; maps and sets sorted by canonical key bytes; every variable-length field length-prefixed (u64 LE length ‖ bytes); ints as sign byte ‖ big-endian magnitude, length-prefixed (arbitrary precision — curve coordinates are 60–254-bit); strings UTF-8 NFC; blob references as `(hash, size)`; NO unknown fields (a key the schema does not declare raises `CanonError` at write time); no floats in keys (numeric profiles are declared as rationals or strings).
- Hash: BLAKE3-256 over `domain_tag ‖ canonical_bytes`. Fixed domain tags: `cairn/recipe-key/v1`, `cairn/hypothesis-key/v1`, `cairn/node/v1`, `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`, `cairn/env-manifest/v1`, `cairn/selftest-cert/v1`, `cairn/gate-bundle/v1`, `cairn/instance/v1` (the verifier instance `(p,a,b,n,P,Q)` — cairn-m0-e0s.8 and .14 hash it with this tag), `cairn/chain/v1` (reserved for M2).
- Recipe key = H over `(skill_identity_hash, inputs: sorted map name → (hash,size), seed, tool_versions: sorted map, container_digest, salt)`. `skill_identity_hash` = hash of the §2 identity bundle `{interface_version, implementation_revision, tool_digests, container_digest, numeric_profile}` so a changed executable is a different recipe. On the M0 machine (no container) `container_digest` = hash of the environment manifest `{os: sw_vers+uname, python, cypari2, libpari (pari.version()), blake3, gp_binary_sha256}` — never empty (empty raises).
- Hypothesis key = H over the typed hypothesis object `{target_family, claimed_property_or_cost_model (or claim statement hash), method_identity (interface version + canonical params — NEVER implementation revision), declared_parameter_ranges, sampling_distribution?}`; per-run seeds, ladder instances and free-text fields are excluded by schema.
- Schemas: one `Schema` (ordered tuple of (name, type)) per object kind; encode walks the schema, never the dict, so undeclared keys surface as a set difference.
- Known-answer vectors `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` (≥6): recipe key (two logically-equal spellings with different dict/set order → same expected hash), hypothesis key, identity bundle, env manifest (fixed synthetic values), node hash, and a negative vector (one byte changed in the canonical input → a DIFFERENT expected hash, asserted not-equal). Generated once, committed; origin recorded `author_supplied` (they pin the encoding against drift; they are not an external oracle).
- `uv run cairn kat canon` runs the KAT and exits 0/1, logging one record per vector (name, expected, computed, match) — the entry bead m0-gate-plan-selftests (cairn-m0-e0s.11) calls.
- Tests (`tests/unit/test_canon.py`): permuting insertion order never changes the hash; undeclared field raises; empty container digest raises; ints round-trip through a decoder used only by tests; every vector matches; the same object under two different domain tags hashes differently.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_canon.py -q` green; `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` committed; `uv run cairn kat canon` prints PASS, exit 0, one log record per vector.
- Planted negative: the negative KAT vector must NOT match; an undeclared field must raise `CanonError`; an empty `container_digest` must raise; two domain tags over one object must not collide. Once at close: flip one byte in a stored vector locally, confirm the KAT test fails, revert; record in the close comment.
- No-Claim: KATs are self-generated; green proves stability of this encoding, not agreement with any external standard; collision resistance is BLAKE3's claim.

title: M0: substrate store (SQLite + BLAKE3): nodes/blobs/lineage, recipes, attempts, execution receipts, cache bits, statuses, salt, disowned, replay grade, certificate slot; single writer + WAL; M1 column fixtures
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): a result not in the substrate does not exist to the claims DB. Provenance is a storage property: every launch appends an attempt; nothing is overwritten; a cached value is served only from a verified attempt; a failure is a record, not a memo. This schema is the shape every later milestone plugs into.

WHAT (`src/cairn/substrate.py`, SQL in `src/cairn/schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3)
Tables
- `blobs(hash PK, size, bytes, created_at)` — the only collectable kind (bead m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- `nodes(hash PK, kind, canonical BLOB, replay_grade CHECK IN ('Replayable','Verifiable','AuditOnly'), producer_identity, created_at)`; `lineage(child_hash, parent_hash, edge_kind)` append-only. Every content-addressed object of any typed table (claims layer included, cairn-m0-e0s.5) also has a `nodes` row with the same hash and kind, so lineage and GC see one graph.
- `roots(root_kind CHECK IN ('recipe','ledger_row','certificate','divergence'), node_hash, PRIMARY KEY(root_kind,node_hash))` — the GC roots table (§3: recipes, ledger rows, certificates and recorded divergences are roots); defined here because `mark_non_reproducible` below roots both attempts; reachability and collection are cairn-m0-e0s.13.
- `recipes(recipe_key PK, skill_identity_hash, inputs_manifest_hash, seed, tool_versions_hash, container_digest, salt, do_not_cache INT)`; inserting a recipe also inserts its `roots('recipe', recipe_key)` row.
- `attempts(attempt_id PK, recipe_key, output_manifest_hash NULL, receipt_hash NULL, status CHECK IN ('RUNNING','OK','FAIL','DISAGREE','BUDGET_EXCEEDED','SKILL_YANKED','INTERRUPTED'), replay_grade, verifier_result_hash NULL, certificate_hash NULL, skip_cache_lookup INT, disowned_at NULL, inadmissible INT DEFAULT 0, started_at, ended_at NULL)`. `RUNNING` is the in-flight status an attempt is inserted with (`ended_at IS NULL`); exactly one UPDATE is permitted per row — `RUNNING` → a terminal status, setting `ended_at`, `output_manifest_hash`, `receipt_hash` together (the runner, cairn-m0-e0s.9, performs it; its `startup_scan()` performs `RUNNING` → `INTERRUPTED` for every row with `ended_at IS NULL` before any new launch, PLAN §4); a second UPDATE raises.
- `receipts(receipt_hash PK, gate_bundle_hash, start_mono, end_mono, cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s, wall_s, peak_rss_bytes, scratch_bytes_written, exit_status, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, tool_digests_hash)` — written by the harness writer only (bead m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9).
- `skill_certificates(identity_bundle_hash PK REFERENCES nodes(hash), cert_hash UNIQUE, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` — the §2 certificate slot; `selftest_summary` is canonical JSON `{corpus_origins: [per-case per-field origins], randomized_arm: bool, cross_check: {axis, independent_range} | null, pass, floor}` that `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12); rows are written by the skill self-test (cairn-m0-e0s.7), which first persists the identity bundle itself as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle', canonical = the §2 bundle bytes)` so every `skill_identity_hash` a recipe, attempt or ticket names resolves to a stored object (a certificate row naming an identity with no `nodes` row is refused); the certificate's own content-addressed object is `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` with a lineage edge `cert_hash → identity_bundle_hash` (`edge_kind = 'certifies'`), and inserting one also inserts `roots('certificate', cert_hash)`. `cert_hash = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)`, each field length-prefixed per cairn-m0-e0s.3 — the identity hash is inside the certificate, so a certificate copied from one revision's row onto another's cannot verify. Predicates here: `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a row exists AND `cert_hash` recomputed from the row's own fields equals the stored one (a tampered or transplanted row is uncertified); `yanked(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a `yank_records` row names it. The tier gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) reads both.
- `yank_records(yank_id, skill_identity_hash, reach_predicate, ruling_ref NULL, record_digest, file_offset, created_at)`, `salts(class_key PK, salt, record_digest, file_offset)` — schema only at M0; both are human-path records (operator decision 5: yanks and salt issuance are human-only, like waivers), hence the attestation digest+offset columns that cairn-m0-e0s.10's `attestation_record_matches` reads at M1.
- `escrow(attempt_id PK, declared_production_cost, declared_verification_cost, reserved, spent_at NULL, released_at NULL, ceiling_multiplier)` — M0 writes and reads every column in a fixture; enforcement is M1 (§13).
Behavior
- Cache serve path `serve(recipe_key)`: the most recent attempt with status OK, not disowned, not inadmissible, recipe not `do_not_cache`, every referenced blob present (else None → recompute). `status ≠ OK ⇒ never cached` is part of the serve query, not a convention (RUNNING, FAIL, DISAGREE, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, SKILL_YANKED, INTERRUPTED are all excluded by that one predicate). `skip_cache_lookup` callers always record a fresh attempt.
- Replayable recipe with two OK, non-disowned attempts whose output manifests differ → `mark_non_reproducible(recipe_key)`: both attempts kept, both rooted (`roots('divergence', attempt output node)`), both `inadmissible=1`.
- Immutability: `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers → `RAISE(ABORT,'append-only')` on nodes, recipes, receipts, lineage, roots, skill_certificates, yank_records, salts; on attempts the only permitted UPDATEs are (i) the single RUNNING→terminal close, (ii) the one-time NULL→value set of `disowned_at`, (iii) the one-time 0→1 set of `inadmissible`; any other UPDATE and every DELETE raises.
- Single writer: `Substrate.open(path, role='writer'|'reader')`; writer sets `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL`; reader opens `file:...?mode=ro` URI; one writer object per process (module guard). Workers never receive the writer.
- `weaken_grade(node_hash, to)`: a grade moves only down the order Replayable > Verifiable > AuditOnly and the move is a new append-only `grade_history(seq PK AUTOINCREMENT, node_hash, from_grade, to_grade, reason, at)` row — `nodes.replay_grade` is never updated in place (the append-only trigger forbids it); `effective_grade(node_hash)` = the latest `grade_history` row's `to_grade`, else the node's column, and every grade reader (`justify`'s AuditOnly rule, the tier gate's ticket rule) reads `effective_grade`; a strengthening, or a move to the same grade, raises.
- Every write and every serve decision logs through `cairn.log` (table, hash, status / served-or-why-not).
TESTS (integration, file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode` asserted `wal`): `weaken_grade` Replayable→Verifiable then →AuditOnly succeeds and `effective_grade` follows while `nodes.replay_grade` is unchanged; AuditOnly→Verifiable raises; Verifiable→Verifiable raises; a certificate row whose `cert_hash`/`transcript_hash`/`env_manifest_hash` are copied from another identity's certified row makes `certified()` false (transplant); a certificate row naming an identity_bundle_hash with no `nodes` row is refused; recipe + OK then FAIL attempts → serve returns the OK manifest; disown the OK attempt → None; `do_not_cache` recipe never serves; `skip_cache_lookup` records a new attempt on a hit; two differing OK manifests → both kept, rooted, inadmissible, serve None; a RUNNING attempt is never served; UPDATE on `attempts.status` of a closed attempt raises; DELETE on a node raises; `disowned_at` settable once; reader connection write → OperationalError readonly; a missing blob makes serve return None; `certified()` true after a well-formed certificate row, false for an unknown identity and false for a row whose `cert_hash` was written tampered; `yanked()` true after a yank_records row; M1-column fixture (`tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py`): every column of `escrow`, `yank_records`, `salts` written and read back byte-equal; one attempt each at `SKILL_YANKED`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `INTERRUPTED` inserted and never served; a `disowned_at` mark excludes its attempt from serve.
DESIGN: SQL in one file; thin typed Python functions; no ORM; insert recomputes the content hash from the canonical bytes and asserts it equals the caller's hash.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_substrate.py tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py -q` green against a real file DB; test log shows `journal_mode=wal`; `certified()`/`yanked()` predicates exercised as named.
- Planted negative: UPDATE to a closed attempt's status must raise (append-only trigger); a FAIL attempt and a RUNNING attempt must never be served; a recipe with a missing blob must not be served (delete one blob row, assert None); a certificate row with a tampered `cert_hash` must make `certified()` false; a transplanted certificate row (fields copied from another identity's row) must make `certified()` false; a strengthening `weaken_grade` must raise. Each asserted as an expected failure.
- No-Claim: M0 proves the schema admits and refuses what §3 names; budget ceiling, escrow spend/release, yank reach and disowned propagation are column fixtures only — their behavior is M1's; `certified()` attests a recorded certificate, not correctness.
notes: BEAD ALIASES → IDS (the descriptions name beads by alias; these are the br ids): m0-scaffold-smoke = cairn-m0-e0s.1; m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2; m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4; m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5; m0-toy-curve-skill = cairn-m0-e0s.6; m0-skill-selftest-cert = cairn-m0-e0s.7; m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8; m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9; m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13; m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14; m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15; m1-ladder = cairn-m1-cqt.1; m1-baseline-skills = cairn-m1-cqt.2; m1-planted-corpus = cairn-m1-cqt.3; m1-budget-escrow-yank = cairn-m1-cqt.4; m1-formalization-gate = cairn-m1-cqt.5; m1-worker-dispatch-canary = cairn-m1-cqt.6; m1-human-queue-review = cairn-m1-cqt.7; m1-router-ledger-hunt-repro = cairn-m1-cqt.8.

title: M0: claims-layer schema: hypothesis object, claim statement node, typed evidence node, append-only tag history, review_verdict (digest+offset), gate-run record, tickets, TierRefused
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §7): the tag is derived, never set; every tag, verdict and gate record names an exact content-addressed statement hash; a human verdict enters through one route and is absent unless its digest matches the attestation file. M0 lays these objects down so `justify`, the tier gate and (from M1) the ladder write to one shape.

WHAT (`src/cairn/claims.py`; additions to `schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; every typed row below also inserts a `nodes` row with the same hash and kind, cairn-m0-e0s.4)
- `hypothesis_objects(hash PK, canonical, claim_statement_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, created_at)` immutable.
- `claim_statements(hash PK, claim_id, version, informal, formal_source NULL, scope, quantities, source_claim_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, status CHECK IN ('open','refuted','promoted','withdrawn'), created_at)` — `scope` is the typed record `{target_family (categorical), size_interval, param_ranges (axis-aligned intervals), assumption_set (content-addressed ids)}`; `quantities` is a typed record carrying, among its units, an optional `cost_model {exponent, constant, crossover}` — `cost_model IS NOT NULL` is what "a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model" means to `justify` (cairn-m0-e0s.12); immutable except a single open→terminal status transition (trigger refuses a second).
- `evidence_nodes(hash PK, kind CHECK IN ('lean_artifact','ladder_table','repro_node','counterexample_hunt_record','statistical','model_proof'), target_statement_hash, population, assumptions, producer_identity, producer_tag, verdict NULL, in_sample_sizes NULL, attempt_id NULL, repro_record_hash NULL, created_at)` — `population` is the same typed record shape as `scope`; `verdict` is the table's/hunt's verdict (`KEEP | KEEP_IN_SAMPLE | REJECT | INCONCLUSIVE | SURVIVED | KILLED | INCOMPLETE`); `in_sample_sizes` is the size interval a `ladder_table` measured in-sample (NULL for other kinds; the KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scope rule in `justify` reads it).

title: M0: exemplar skill toy_curve(bits, seed) → (p,a,b,n,P) on PARI via cypari2: algorithm-axis cross-check (≤50 bits), postcondition arm, declared cost profile measured over ≥50 seeds, content-addressed I/O
description:
WHY (PLAN §2, §13): the exemplar is the one skill built end to end at M0 — typed interface, fixed version, content-addressed I/O, captured seed, self-test, declared cost profile; every research skill from M1 copies its shape. Operator decision 1: PARI-only at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check valid for bits ≤ 50; no second implementation until M1 (gmpy2).

INTERFACE (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`): `run(bits: int, seed: int) -> ToyCurveOutput{p, a, b, n, P=(x,y), tries, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:'bits<=50', result:'agree'|'untested'}, status:'OK'|'DISAGREE'}`. Declared cost profile `{tier: 0, production: 'c·ln p tries; c per size from the measured table', verification: 'Replayable, Tier-0 re-run'}`; replay grade Replayable; `do_not_cache=False`. Module entry `python -m cairn.skills.toy_curve` reads canonical JSON inputs on stdin and writes canonical JSON output on stdout (the runner contract, bead m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9); the skill never opens the substrate and receives no substrate path.

ALGORITHM — CALL SEQUENCE PINNED (matches the grounding brief's bench.gp / bench_cypari2.py, which gave bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries in gp and cypari2; the PARI PRNG state is part of the contract — probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4: at 40 bits `ellcard(E)` leaves the PRNG state unchanged while `ellsea(E)` advances it, and at 60 bits both `ellcard(E)` and `ellsea(E,1)` advance it, so any call added inside the loop, or reordered after it, changes every later draw): `setrand(seed)`; `p = randomprime([2^(bits-1), 2^bits])`; `tries = 0`; loop: `a = random(p); b = random(p)`; if `4a³+27b² ≡ 0 (mod p)` continue (a singular pair is not counted); `tries += 1`; `E = ellinit([a,b], p)`; bits ≤ 50 → `n = ellcard(E)` (generic path, milliseconds), accept iff `isprime(n)`; bits > 50 → `m = ellsea(E,1)` (early abort: returns 0 on a small factor), accept iff `m ≠ 0 and isprime(m)`, with `n = m`. After the loop, in this order: bits > 50 only — confirm `ellcard(E) == n` once under the 64 MB stack (a mismatch is `status='DISAGREE'` exactly like the cross-check below, though at 60 bits both calls are SEA and no independence is claimed); then `P = random(E)` (non-identity); then the postcondition arm; then, bits ≤ 50 only, the algorithm-axis cross-check — after P is drawn and never inside the loop. Expected tries for seeds 1,2,3 (the bench rows; the integration test asserts them): 30 bits 48/148/20; 40 bits 40/52/57; 50 bits 36/11/220; 60 bits 45/72/140. All order calls go through the `cairn.pari.ellcard` / `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrappers (cairn-m0-e0s.1) — the one seam where a test plants a disagreement.
Algorithm-axis cross-check (bits ≤ 50 only, once, on the accepted curve): `ellsea(E)` (SEA) must equal `ellcard(E)` (generic BSGS-family); on mismatch return `status='DISAGREE'` (never OK, never cached) carrying both transcripts and digests for a substrate node; NO silent retry with a third tool. For bits > 50 `result='untested'` (at 60 bits `ellcard` is itself SEA — agreement by construction, no independence claimed). A cross-check that has never disagreed is reported in the self-test ledger as untested-for-disagreement, never as passing.
Randomized postcondition arm on every output: `isprime(n)`; `ellmul(E,P,n)==[0]`; `n ∈ [p+1-2√p, p+1+2√p]`; `ellisoncurve(E,P)`.
Content-addressed I/O: inputs `{bits, seed}` canonicalized; output manifest = canonical bytes of the output hashed (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3).
Cost-profile constant: `uv run cairn measure toy-curve-tries --sizes 30,40,50,60 --seeds 50` records tries for ≥50 seeds per size (60 bits included: the skill's declared range reaches the 60-bit rung and its per-try cost there is the `ellsea(E,1)` early-abort path at ≈ 0.3 ms per rejected curve, so 50 seeds finish in well under a minute; the constant is declared per size) (mean, sd, min, max, wall) into its own section of `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md`; the declared profile cites that table (STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the sample), never the 3-seed table (20–220 tries; CONJECTURE on means). Expected shape: geometric, sd ≈ mean, expected tries ≈ c·ln p.
Stack: `cairn.pari` applies `allocatemem(64_000_000)` once before any 60-bit work.
Logging: every run logs (bits, seed, tries, n bit-length, cross_check result, status, wall) through `cairn.log`; a DISAGREE logs both transcript digests.
TESTS (integration, real cypari2): seeds 1,2,3 at 30/40/50 bits reproduce the grounding brief's (p,a,b,n,tries) rows bit-for-bit (pins cypari2-vs-gp agreement and the call sequence); 60-bit seeds 1,2,3 complete via ellsea(E,1)+ellcard within a minute each with tries 45/72/140 (the brief's mode-1 rows), and seed 1 equals the committed `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) field for field; a call-order guard: a spy on the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper asserts it is invoked exactly once per ≤ 50-bit run and only after the accepted curve's P is drawn (an invocation inside the loop, or a second one, fails the test); postcondition arm asserted on every output; double run same seed → byte-identical manifests; different seed → different p; DISAGREE path via the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper monkeypatched to return n+2 at 40 bits → status DISAGREE, both transcripts present, no OK output; singular pair skipped; forced composite n fails the postcondition arm; unit test (`tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py`): the stdin/stdout JSON contract round-trips a fixed output and rejects a malformed input with a typed error before any PARI call.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py -q` green: 30/40/50-bit outputs for seeds 1–3 equal the grounding-brief rows (p,a,b,n,tries); double run byte-equal; 60-bit seeds 1–3 return prime n with cross_check.result='untested' and tries 45/72/140, seed 1 equal to `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json`; the ≥50-seeds-per-size measurement table (30/40/50/60 bits) is committed in research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md and the declared profile cites it.
- Planted negative: monkeypatched `ellsea` wrapper → n+2 must yield status DISAGREE with both transcripts and no OK; a singular pair must be skipped; a forced composite n must fail the postcondition arm; a malformed stdin input must be refused before any PARI call; a cross-check call planted inside the search loop must break tries reproduction and trip the call-order guard. Each asserted.
- No-Claim: gp/cypari2 agreement is one library twice (one implementation) — it proves the binding, not the arithmetic; the algorithm cross-check is independent only for bits ≤ 50; the measured constant is for this machine and these sizes.

title: M0: toy_curve self-test: vendored known-answer corpus (4 cases, origin per field) + ledger + pass floor, randomized_postcondition arm, golden certificate, byte-equal double run, certificate recorded → revision certified
description:
WHY (PLAN §2): a skill's self-test is (i) a vendored known-answer corpus with a per-case ledger `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap` and a committed pass floor only an attributed update may raise; (ii) a golden certificate = hash over the canonical transcript of the corpus and the exact outputs — a changed implementation behind the same interface needs a fresh certificate and a mismatch fails closed; (iii) every nondeterminism source pinned and a byte-equal double run asserted. A corpus supplied only by the author is not a self-test (`author_supplied` alone caps results at CONJECTURE, enforced by `justify`'s producer-standing rule). A revision is launchable only once its self-test passed and its certificate is recorded; the tier gate refuses an uncertified revision exactly as a yanked one.

CORPUS (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`, origin per field; sources pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §4). Origin rule: a field copied from an upstream document is `upstream_vendored`; a field completed locally (a point chosen here, a scalar or Q computed here) is `author_supplied` and is re-checked by a postcondition at every self-test run — it is never trusted; the `randomized_postcondition` origin names only the seeded arm below (inputs drawn from a seed committed after the implementation revision is content-addressed).
1. F_5: `y² = x³ − 3x + 1`, `n = 7` — `upstream_vendored` (PARI 2.17.4 usersch3.tex:29031-29032). `P=(0,1)`, `Q=3P=(3,3)`, `x=3` derived locally — origin `author_supplied`; every self-test run asserts `ellorder(E,P)=7` and `ellmul(E,P,3)=Q`; never trusted as vendored (PLAN §13: a locally completed triple is author_supplied).
2. GF(101): `y² = x³ + 90x + 44`, `n = 89` (prime), `x = 2`, `Q = 2P` — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4529-4537 + constructor.py:790-791). `P` is not explicit upstream (`E.gens()[0]`) → chosen locally as the least-x non-identity point; origin `author_supplied` for P with the per-run postcondition `ellorder(E,P)=89`, `2P=Q`.
3. 150-bit: `p = 1427247692705959881058285969449495136382746771`, `E=[1,1]`, `P=(831623307675610677632782670796608848711856078, 42295786042873366706573292533588638217232964)`, `n = 1427247692705959881058262545272474300628281448` (composite, even) — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4680-4686); membership/cardinality/big-int path; no x.
4. Negative control: `E=[1,0]/GF(419)`, `P=(-33,8)`, order 21, card 420 — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:822-827); asserts `n·Q ≠ O` for a point outside the order-21 subgroup — the must-FAIL fixture of the postcondition.
RANDOMIZED_POSTCONDITION ARM per run: generate a 30-bit curve from a seed committed AFTER the implementation revision is content-addressed (seed = first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')), assert the postcondition arm (`isprime(n)`, `n·P = O`, Hasse interval, on-curve). Verifier-shaped arm on the same curve, run through the real Tier-0 verifier driver (bead m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8, real gp subprocess): 20 draws `x`, `Q = xP` → driver returns OK; 20 draws `x' ≠ x` → FAIL `xP-ne-Q`; both counts are fields of the transcript. This bead owns wiring that arm (dependency on cairn-m0-e0s.8); the verifier's own planted self-test belongs to the gate plan (cairn-m0-e0s.11).
LEDGER + FLOOR: each case → `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; `pass_floor` (M0: 4/4 + both arms) lives in the corpus file; only an attributed change (commit with reason) may raise it.
CERTIFICATE: `transcript` = canonical bytes of (corpus, exact outputs, ledger, arm outcomes); `cert = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)` (each field length-prefixed; the identity hash is inside the certificate, so it cannot be transplanted onto another revision's row); the self-test first persists the identity bundle as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle')`, then writes the `skill_certificates` row `(identity_bundle_hash, cert_hash, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` together with its `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` row, the lineage edge certificate → identity bundle and `roots('certificate', cert_hash)` (table, rows and the `certified()` predicate are bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); `selftest_summary` = `{corpus_origins (per case, per field), randomized_arm: true, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:'bits<=50'}, pass: 4, floor: 4}` — what `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12). DOUBLE RUN: the whole self-test runs twice; canonical transcripts byte-equal (no timestamps inside the transcript; seed, hashers, clock pinned). Runtime target < 5 s, Tier-0.
CLI: `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve [--json]` exits 0 and prints the certificate hash; a corpus schema check requires `origin` on every field; every case and arm logs (case id, ledger entry, observed vs expected) through `cairn.log`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py -q` green; `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve --json` prints `{pass:4, floor:4, arms:{postcondition:'pass', verifier:{ok:20, fail:20}}, certificate:<hash>, double_run:'byte-equal'}`; a `skill_certificates` row exists for the identity bundle hash and `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` is true; `nodes` rows exist for both the identity bundle and the certificate and `roots` holds `('certificate', cert_hash)`; its `selftest_summary` carries the per-field origins (case 1 P/Q/x and case 2 P as `author_supplied`).
- Planted negative: (a) alter one expected output in a temp copy of the corpus → certificate mismatch, exit ≠ 0, `certified()` false; (b) the negative-control point must FAIL `n·Q = O` (if it passes, the test fails); (c) bump `implementation_revision` without re-running → `certified()` false for the new identity hash; (d) the verifier arm's 20 `x' ≠ x` draws must all FAIL (one OK fails the self-test).
- No-Claim: certified ≠ correct beyond the corpus; cases with `author_supplied` fields are capped at CONJECTURE by `justify` only where no covering arm or cross-check exists (the seeded arm and the ≤50-bit cross-check cover this skill); the 150-bit case has no discrete-log component.

title: M0: Tier-0 verifier subprocess (gp): membership n·Q=O then xP==Q; affirmative acceptance (rc==0 AND stdout==OK AND stderr empty); arity/field validation before spawn; explicit stack ceiling; forced crash → FAIL; gate-read instance, submitter supplies x only
description:
WHY: "No submission without a passing verifier (xP == Q) subprocess" is an invariant (CLAUDE.md). Acceptance is affirmative, never residual: gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow — PROVEN by probe) and zero-fills missing arguments, so rc==0 is not evidence of anything. The instance is gate-read: the curve, n, P, Q come from the claim statement node or dispatch record, never from the submitter, who supplies x alone — `xP == Q` on an instance the worker chose is a true statement about the wrong problem (PLAN §4).

WHAT (`src/cairn/verifier.py`, `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`)
- `verify.gp` (shape from grounding brief §3): `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)`: `ispseudoprime(p)` → nonsingular → `ellisoncurve(E,P)` and `(E,Q)` → `ellmul(E,Q,n)==[0]` (membership FIRST — PARI's generic `elllog` can loop when no solution exists; the verifier never calls a log) → `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q`; prints exactly one line `OK` or `FAIL <reason-codes>`; `quit(0|1)`.
- Driver `Verifier.run(instance: Instance, x: int) -> VerifierResult`: validates arity (exactly 9 fields), every field a non-negative int, `Px,Py,Qx,Qy < p`, `x < n`, `n` inside the Hasse interval of p (`|n − (p+1)| ≤ 2√p`) — BEFORE spawning; renders the nine values as decimal integer strings on ONE stdin line `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)` (never hex, never floats); spawns `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",stack_ceiling]` loading `verify.gp` through `cairn.pari.run_gp`; backend path, stack ceiling, timeout and accept predicate come from the gate bundle (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; injected as a config object at unit level); accepts iff `rc==0 AND stdout.strip()=="OK" AND stderr==""` (satisfiable — probed 2026-08-21: `gp -q -f -s 64M verify.gp` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr on a good instance; `quit(1)` gives rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; the 8 MB stack overflow gives rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr); everything else → FAIL with `reason ∈ {p-not-prime, singular, P-off-curve, Q-off-curve, nQ-not-O, xP-ne-Q, backend-crash, timeout, bad-arity, bad-field, submitter-named-instance}` (`backend-crash` covers a stack overflow with rc 0 and a killed child with rc < 0); default timeout 30 s.
- Instance binding: `Instance{p,a,b,n,P,Q}` has `instance_hash = H('cairn/instance/v1' ‖ canonical instance)` (domain tag from cairn-m0-e0s.3); `run` takes an `Instance` produced by the gate run (from the claim statement node / dispatch record) and a bare `x`; a `Submission` carrying its own `(P,Q)` is refused with `reason='submitter-named-instance'` before any subprocess is spawned (a spy asserts zero spawns). The result records `instance_hash`.

title: M0: skill runner: subprocess launch with content-addressed inputs, harness-written execution receipt (CPU/wall/RSS/scratch bytes/exit/digests/bundle hash), attempt row + statuses, cache bits, 4× wall ceiling on the trivial fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §3, §5): the execution receipt is the harness's own record of the run, written by the writer and never by the skill; its readers are the budget ceiling, the ladder's clock and memory measurements and the provenance check. A receipt the skill writes about itself is a number from the gated party. Workers are subprocesses that return artifacts to the single writer and hold no write capability.

WHAT (`src/cairn/runner.py`)
- `launch(skill_identity, inputs, seed, *, bundle_hash, scratch_dir, declared_expectation_s, budget_remaining) -> Attempt`: computes the recipe key (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); honors cache bits (`skip_cache_lookup`, `do_not_cache`, serve path of bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); inserts the attempt row with status `RUNNING` (cairn-m0-e0s.4); spawns the skill as a subprocess (`[sys.executable, "-m", "cairn.skills.<name>"]`, canonical JSON in on stdin, canonical JSON out on stdout, scratch path passed as an argument; the child receives NO substrate path or handle and an environment scrubbed of `CAIRN_DB*`); waits with `os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)` for rusage (ru_utime, ru_stime, ru_maxrss) and takes the exit status from the status word it returns (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode`), setting `proc.returncode` itself and never calling `proc.wait()`/`proc.poll()` afterwards — CPython's `Popen._try_wait` turns the `ChildProcessError` of an already-reaped child into status 0 (subprocess.py, read 2026-08-21 on Python 3.14.3), which would record every crash as exit 0; `time.monotonic()` start/end; wall; bytes written under scratch (directory-size delta); exit status; stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; tool digests (gp sha256, cypari2/libpari versions); bundle hash. Writes the receipt node and closes the attempt row (the single RUNNING→terminal UPDATE) with status: `OK` (exit 0, well-formed output, skill status OK); `FAIL` (non-zero exit, malformed output, or skill status FAIL); `DISAGREE` (skill status DISAGREE); `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (wall past `ceiling = multiplier × declared_expectation_s`, multiplier 4× from the bundle (CONJECTURE, §5) → child killed). `startup_scan()` moves every `RUNNING` attempt with NULL `ended_at` to `INTERRUPTED` before any new launch (M0 implements the scan; M3 exercises it under crash tests).
- Output manifest: each artifact a blob (hash,size); manifest node linked to the attempt; lineage edges attempt → inputs.
- Escrow: writes the reservation columns at launch (schema-only at M0; reserve/spend/release behavior is M1).
- Logging: each launch logs (recipe key, served-from-cache | spawned, argv at DEBUG, status, wall_ms, cpu_s, rss) through `cairn.log`; a kill logs the ceiling and the elapsed wall.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_runner.py`; the launch subject is the real `toy_curve` skill, cairn-m0-e0s.6): launch toy_curve 40-bit seed 1 → attempt OK; receipt has cpu>0, wall>0, rss>0, stdout_digest == BLAKE3 of captured stdout; output manifest hash equals the skill's own manifest; second identical launch → served from cache, no new attempt; with `skip_cache_lookup` → new attempt, same manifest (Replayable double-attempt agreement); fixture skill exiting 3 → FAIL attempt, never served, and its receipt's `exit_status == 3` (a status read through Popen after the wait4 reap would be 0); fixture sleeping 2 s with declared expectation 0.2 s → killed at 0.8 s, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, never served, its receipt's `exit_status` carrying the kill signal; fixture emitting a `receipt` key in its output → ignored (receipt.cpu differs from the fake); fixture that prints its environment → no substrate path visible; `startup_scan()` on a DB with an unfinished RUNNING attempt marks it INTERRUPTED and a later `serve` ignores it.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_runner_status.py`, no subprocess): the status mapping table (exit, stdout well-formedness, skill status, wall vs ceiling) → exactly one of OK/FAIL/DISAGREE/BUDGET_EXCEEDED; ceiling arithmetic (`4 × 0.2 s = 0.8 s`); the environment scrub removes every `CAIRN_DB*` variable.
